def _unique_path(directory: Path, filename: str) -> Path:
    dest = directory / filename
    if not dest.exists():
        return dest
    stem = Path(filename).stem
    suffix = Path(filename).suffix
    counter = 2
    while True:
        dest = directory / f"{stem}_{counter}{suffix}"
        if not dest.exists():

        counter += 1

@router.get("/stream")
async def stream_fight_state(request: Request):
    async def event_generator():
        q: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
        register_queue(q)
        try:
            snapshot = await asyncio.to_thread(fight_service.get_all_fights)
            data = json.dumps([
                {"id": f.id, "state": f.state} for f in snapshot
            ])
            yield f"event: snapshot\ndata: {data}\n\n"

            while True:

                    break
                try:
                    payload = await asyncio.wait_for(q.get(), timeout=15.0)
                    yield f"data: {payload}\n\n"
                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                    yield ": ping\n\n"
        finally:
            unregister_queue(q)

    return StreamingResponse(

        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={

---
name: corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground
description: "eval/corner_accuracy.py reads the shorts band as a fraction of bbox height, so it goes nearly blind on ground/clinch frames — a low decisive-frame count is \"unverified\", not \"fine\""
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 53047172-e54e-4eb1-a0f1-31064b2e9209
  modified: 2026-08-23T07:32:54.047Z
---

`ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py` samples each fighter's shorts band at
`_BAND_TOP=0.42` to `_BAND_BOTTOM=0.72` **of bbox height**. That geometry only
lands on the trunks when the fighter is upright. On the ground the bbox goes
wide-and-short and the band slices across arms, canvas and the opponent, so
`_colour_vote` almost never clears `_MIN_COLOUR_PX` / `_MIN_DECISIVENESS`.

Measured 2026-08-23 on DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA (a ground-heavy fight, 83 of 163 hand
labels are `ground_punch`), frames 1199–34767 at stride 15 (~2200 frames
sampled):

- fight 48 (old pipeline): **7** decisive frames
- fight 52 (new pipeline): **3** decisive frames

Whole-fight at stride 10 the same fight yields 55 decisive frames — i.e. the
evidence comes almost entirely from the standing portions elsewhere in the video.

**Why:** a whole-fight accuracy number is therefore not evenly distributed over
the fight. It can read "56% correct" while contributing essentially zero
evidence about the ground exchanges, which is exactly where tracker identity
swaps are most likely and where corner errors do the most damage to training
data.

**How to apply:** treat a low decisive-frame count as *unverified*, never as a
pass — the module's own docstring says this for the zero case and the same
applies at n=3. For ground-heavy footage, verify corners by eye
(`--verify-pose` overlay video) or via labeller-marked `corner_swap` spans

name: corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps
description: "assign_corners' hysteresis barrier is charged twice, so a tracker identity swap is mathematically uncorrectable without visible glove tape."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fbf2c258-92a1-4a58-8ba1-d5ff99286f32
  modified: 2026-08-30T09:58:15.667Z
---

Measured 2026-08-30. In `assign_corners._assign_frame_labels`, `_cost` adds
`CORNER_HYSTERESIS_WEIGHT` (0.5) per detection whose label would flip. A corner
swap always flips both slots, so the barrier is **1.0**. Evidence per detection
is `CORNER_TAPE_WEIGHT` (0.6) × tape + `CORNER_HIST_WEIGHT` (0.4) × hist, and
when no glove tape is visible `_tape_distance_term` returns exactly 0.5 for both
corners (confidence factor 0), so the tape term cancels. Torso histogram alone
can therefore move the two-detection total by at most **0.8 < 1.0**: the flip
can never win. In practice Bhattacharyya gaps give ~0.16–0.32, versus a 1.0
barrier.

The single-detection branch charges the barrier only **once** (0.5), so a
one-sided observation faces a *lower* bar than both fighters seen together —
backwards, since it is the weaker evidence.

**Why:** this is the only mechanism that can repair a `FighterTracker` identity
swap, and it is disabled exactly when the gloves aren't visible — which is most
of a clinch and most of a ground sequence.

**How to apply:** charge the barrier once per *mapping* decision (it is a
bijection — see the atomic-commit note already in ai/CLAUDE.md), consistently in
both branches, before touching the constant's value. Note the deeper issue too:
the mapping is global, so it cannot represent a swap that lasts only from one
camera cut to the next, and the run logs show it flip-flopping 444–813 times per
fight chasing local errors with a global boolean. See
[[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]] and
[[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].

name: easyocr-confidence-is-noise
description: "EasyOCR line confidence on fight-ai scoreboard crops is noise-dominated (median ±0.117 from a 1px ROI change), so it cannot carry a tight threshold"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

Measured 2026-08-17 on `DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA.mp4`: re-OCRing the *same* scoreboard
digits under a ≤1px change to the calibrated ROI moves EasyOCR's line
confidence by a **median of 0.117, max 0.433**. 30% of correct timer readings
straddle 0.7. So `SCOREBOARD_OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE` gates on a quantity noisier
than any increment worth tuning, and there is a feedback loop: calibration only
unions boxes clearing the floor, so changing the floor changes the ROI, which
changes the confidences again.

**Why:** it means "tune the OCR confidence threshold" is never the right
framing for a scoreboard-coverage problem — the number is not measuring
reading quality. What actually rejects bad reads is structural: the
seconds>59/minutes>59 range check in `parsers.py` and the clock-intercept fit
in `fight_segmentation.py`.

**How to apply:** to check whether a timer read is real, don't look at
confidence — compute `k = frame/fps + seconds_remaining` and test whether it
agrees with the round's intercept. Real reads cluster within ~0.5s (the 2 Hz
sampling quantum); misreads land far off. This is a label-free correctness
check and is how the 0.7→0.5 change was validated over 4781 samples with zero
false reads. See [[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]].

`backend/app/services/label_span_service.py:10-34` seeds `label_spans` of kind
`round` from the `rounds` table (AI segmentation output) the first time the
Annotate page requests them, so the labeller starts pre-filled. If nobody edits
them, the "ground truth" is byte-identical to the prediction.

As of 2026-08-17 that was true of fight 46 (DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA) — 3 spans, one
shared microsecond-identical `created_at`, `labeled_at` NULL, 0 strike events,
and `segmentation_needs_review = true` with a reason calling the boundaries
"a guess". Fight 42 also matched AI output exactly; only fight 44 had a
human-adjusted round start.

**Why:** scoring round IoU against seeded spans reads 1.000 before any change
and makes every genuine segmentation *improvement* look like a regression.

**How to apply:** before trusting a round-IoU number, check whether the label
span differs from the `rounds` row and whether the span timestamps are
distinct. `eval.cli export` refuses fights with `labeled_at IS NULL`, which
catches the unfinished case but *not* the seeded-then-finished case.
Also note 3 of 4 fights were processed on the manual-labeling track and have
zero `fight_events`, so strike P/R/F1 is structurally 0 for them.

As of 2026-08-06, Filip and I agreed a staged plan to fix fight-ai's unreliable

- **Stage 0 (in progress)** — build an eval harness before changing anything.
  Lives in `ai/eval/` (labelling tool, scorer, label-free sanity checks).
  Target ~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights.

  proposals approach, accepting that it is blocked on labelling first.

cannot be made reliable by more tuning — several constants are compensating for
bugs elsewhere rather than describing anything physical.

**How to apply:** don't propose VLM-based detection for the strike/state
problem — that fork was considered and declined. Don't change a threshold in
`constants.py` without a before/after `python -m eval.cli score` number.

Measured 2026-08-30 against the labeller's own `label_spans` of kind
`corner_swap` — these are the ground truth for identity swaps and need no
re-run to use. Fight 54 has 8 spans (6–35 s each), fight 52 has 5 (1.7–8.7 s).

Against a 5000-frame random control per fight, window ±6 frames:
- **fight 54 span STARTS**: 4/8 in the top decile of frame-to-frame box jump
  (chance 1.5) — a camera switch.
- **fight 54 span ENDS**: 4/7 in the top decile of inter-fighter box IoU
  (chance 1.5).
- **fight 52 span STARTS**: median inter-fighter IoU 0.73 vs control 0.00 — a
  clinch.

Both entry points are where `FighterTracker`'s geometry-only cost is
uninformative. n is small (5 and 8 spans), so treat this as directional.

Two structural facts behind it: nothing in `ai/` detects a shot boundary at all
(grep for cut/shot/scene finds only prose), and `FighterTracker._assign` has **no
maximum-cost gate** — only the Hungarian padding cells carry the 1e6 sentinel, so
a detection anywhere in the frame will always match some slot rather than letting
the slot coast.

A global HSV-histogram cut detector is the wrong instrument here: it found only
29 cuts in 47k frames of fight 54, because broadcast MMA cuts between cameras
pointed at the same cage barely change the global histogram. Use the geometric
signal (simultaneous box jump) instead.

**Why:** a swap that enters at a cut persists until the next one, because
`assign_corners` can only apply a global flip — see
[[corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps]].

**How to apply:** measure any tracking change against these spans rather than by
eye, and check the run log first — on fight 54 the appearance path was skipped
entirely (`ambiguous tape (both slots read blue)`), so the static legacy map ran
and no swap was corrected at all.

`excluded` therefore survives for one narrow purpose: **mid-round replays and
camera cuts away from the cage.** Between-round replays are already outside the
rounds. A rare annotation, but a real one.

"Fully annotated" ([0c(2)](02b-label-schema.md#0c-2)) = every round's full span

`LABELING_COMPLETE` and setting `labeled_at`.

### Corner override

The labeller **can** override corner assignment, and does it by marking a
`corner_swap` span: "from here to here, red and blue are flipped." A whole-video
flip is just a span covering everything — no special case.

This beats excluding the bad span, because clinch frames are where the pipeline
is worst and therefore the most valuable training data; excluding them discards
exactly what the model most needs.

**Do not mutate `fighter_frames`.** Those rows are pipeline *output*. Correcting
them in place destroys the evidence of how often corner assignment was wrong,
which [Stage 1](03-stage1-artifacts.md) needs to measure. Predictions stay
immutable, corrections are stored as labels, and the flip is applied at export
time when joining labels to keypoints. A metric falls out for free: **fraction
of labelled frames covered by a `corner_swap` span = the pipeline's
corner-assignment error rate** — a *lower bound* on it, strictly, since it
counts only the swaps a human caught. [0g](02d-label-quality.md#0g) measures
that recall and replaces the bound with a real figure.

### How span annotation works

All three kinds are **start/end toggles**: one key at the playhead to open the
span, one to close it. A handful per fight. `round` spans arrive pre-seeded from
segmentation, so the labeller is usually adjusting rather than creating.

**Why state stays as change-points** (already the case, worth preserving): you
do not mark "clinch from 3001 to 3400"; you mark *"clinch starts here"*, then
later *"striking starts here"*, and the span is derived — each mark runs to the
next. This matches how state actually behaves (the fight is always in exactly one
state) and halves the interaction: one keystroke per transition rather than two
per span.

Correction happens on the existing **`AnnotationTimeline`** — add one lane per
span kind, coloured bars, drag the edges to fine-tune. Keyboard marking at the
playhead stays primary; the timeline is for fixing afterwards. Derived state
spans must not overlap; `excluded`, `corner_swap` and `round` may overlap
